elements.text:
Dear Eric,

So LB offers a
subscribe_headers()
and a
subscribe_blocks()
. (accessible by
full_node.chain()

. )
-
Note that the subscribe_header name is totally illogical as really what it does is header reorg listening, it is not just dispatched at the full_node’s reception of just any header.

This is also reflected in the fact that the callback gets the arguments “outgoing” and “incoming” which denote a reorg
-

So these are for listening for two distinct events, we can call them “header reorg” and “block reorg”.

Please explain to me how full_node’s “header reorg” and “block reorg” processes are correlated. Especially, i want to understand, the header reorg callbacks are made *when* in the chain syncing process, and the block reorg callbacks are made *when* in the chain syncing process?

Especially then “when”s in the chain sync that I am interested in is, what if a full_node technically has two HEAD blocks on different forks:

the header sync process may use as HEAD the header of block X.

meanwhile the block sync process may use as HEAD the block Y which is on a different chain from X. this discrepancy would arise when the full_node has full blocks downloaded for genesis ... Y, BUT, it does not have blocks downloaded for genesis ... X yet! (or anyhow in the genesis ... X chain up to a total amount of work bigger than that of Y).

(Please note: subscribe_headers should be renamed to subscribe_header_sync_reorg , the current name is confusing and not relevant.)

elements.text: headers are organized into a chain before blocks are organized. I've described this process previously. this implies that there are two distinct events. these processes run concurrently, as previously described. Potential differences between these chains is not  a discrepancy, it's by design. There is only one genesis block/header, which is defined in configuration. Adding "sync_reorg" to the subscriptions does not differentiate them from anything else, as all header and blocks are only obtained through reorganization. There is no published event when network merely obtains a header or block from a peer. "sync" is not a differentiating concept and "reorg" is where blocks and headers come from (hence the presence of incoming and outgoing on all header/block notifications).

elements.text:
Eric thanks a lot for clarifying!

That is that a full_node’s subscribe_headers() and subscribe_blocks() only regard headers/blocks where the node has a whole header/block chain already that includes covers said header/block.

Apologies if the following appears like asking doubly however I wish to get great clarity on this. To really get it, I’ll describe the context first:


So a node firstly receives block headers. This becomes one whole set Htot, of all headers it received. It’s an array sorted in ascending order of time received.

The node basically calculates a function most_work_header_chain(Htot) -> Hmostwork . Hmostwork is a deterministic function of Htot.

What you are saying then is that subscribe_headers() will produce a callback at any change to Htot.


And then, a node receives blocks. A node will only receive blocks that it has headers for, either by a whole block dropping in in one piece (in which case the header would be added to Htot), or through that a node asks for the block that corresponds to a given header.

Received blocks become one whole set Btot. It’s an array sorted in ascending order of time received.

map(block_get_header,Btot) is always a subset of Htot.

subscribe_blocks() will produce a callback at any change of Btot.


My question to you now is this:

The node tracks a main full blockchain, we can call it Bmostwork.

What is the correlation between Hmostwork and Bmostwork actually???

Please explain.

For instance, is LB implemented in such a way that map(block_get_header,Bmostwork) is always a subset of Hmostwork - I presume **NOT***? Please confirm?

But then, may there be moments when Hmostwork and Bmostwork are different chains altogether?

(As in that Hmostwork does not contain block_get_header(tail(Bmostwork,1)) *AND* map(block_get_header,Bmostwork) does not contain tail(Hmostwork,1). On this one I’m unclear.

Your clarification of how LB does this would be very much appreciated, thanks!

elements.text: Bitcoin headers do not form a linked list (chain), they form a tree. We download blocks for the strongest branch of that tree. This changes when there is a reorg. It may just get longer, or may be entirely replaced all the way to genesis.
